clues: This planned city sits in the centre of the north of its land, just south of a far older city. A wide river flows near it.
Summers are long and hot, and monsoon rains arrive in late June and last to mid September. Winters are cool, with thick fog on many mornings.
In 1911, King George V laid the first stone for a fresh capital south of the old city. Two men drew the plans, and the seat opened in 1931.
Until 1911, the capital sat in Calcutta, a port far to the east. Then the rulers packed up and moved the whole seat to this planned city.
All three branches of the government of India sit in this city. The president's palace and the parliament house both stand here.
